minimal_fix: Immediately after the existing cudaDeviceSynchronize, take an end timestamp on every rank. Compute each elapsed millisecond count and reduce those long values with MPI_LONG and MPI_MAX to rank 0. Print the reduced value under 'Computation time' and use it for the performance calculation. A start barrier is unnecessary for this maximum of complete local durations.
semantic_equivalence_basis: A global-makespan equivalence fails at both boundaries. All ranks receive their complete input before timing. Their first numerical work is computeChemicalPotentialKernel, which evaluates concentration-dependent chemical potentials and Laplacians without further MPI dependencies. It can therefore begin before rank 0's timestamp. Likewise, rank 0's device synchronization does not wait for another rank's kernels. Replicated inputs and identical iteration counts do not prove identical execution times.
notes: This conclusion applies to the supplied four-rank hybrid benchmark configuration, -x 512 -i 100. The supplied target-platform evidence establishes that the millisecond count has type long, matching %ld and the proposed MPI_LONG reduction. Whole-millisecond formatting is not a defect. Device allocation and transfers inside timing are permitted conservative overhead.

evidence.finding: Initialization and the input broadcast occur before timing; rank 0 additionally prints a message before its timestamp. There is no post-start communication gating other ranks' computation.
The first kernel performs useful numerical work by computing chemical potentials from concentration values and their Laplacians.
Every rank independently executes the complete simulation loop. Blocking device-to-host copies and the final cudaDeviceSynchronize establish local GPU completion, but no cross-rank completion.
Only rank 0 stops timing and prints its duration. There is no duration reduction or global completion dependency before reporting; MPI_Finalize follows the report.
Validation and result-output flags do not select a different simulation or timing path.
Optional result printing and validation run only after the canonical time has been measured and reported.
